questions.question: Define slavery and give the dates, main destinations and approximate numbers of the transatlantic slave trade.
questions.expected_answer: Slavery is a system in which people are treated as property, owned by others, forced to work without pay and denied freedom. The transatlantic slave trade lasted from the early 1500s to the second half of the 1800s; about 12.5 million Africans were embarked and about 10.5 million arrived, mostly in Brazil and the Caribbean, with about 400 000 taken directly to North America.

questions.question: Describe three features of slavery in West Africa before the Atlantic trade.
questions.expected_answer: Most enslaved people were war captives (also debt, crime or famine); they worked in farming, households, crafts and even as soldiers or officials; treatment varied; they and especially their children could be gradually integrated into families and communities; it was based on being an outsider, not on race; other forms of servitude such as pawnship existed.

questions.question: Explain three ways the transatlantic slave trade differed from earlier slavery in West Africa, and give one effect of the trade on Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Much larger scale; chattel slavery in which people were owned permanently as property and their children were born enslaved, with little path to freedom or integration; slavery linked to race and justified by racist ideas. Effects on Africa: loss of millions of young people; increased wars and raids fuelled by guns; some states grew powerful while others were devastated; long-term damage to economies and societies.
